title: TDNetGen: Empowering Complex Network Resilience Prediction with Generative Augmentation of Topology and Dynamics

problem.claim: Resilience prediction seeks to determine whether complex networks retain fundamental functionality under external perturbations or internal failures.

gap.claim: Theoretical approaches require prior knowledge of network dynamics, while data-driven approaches often lack sufficient labeled data.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces TDNetGen, a resilience prediction framework using generative augmentation of network topology and dynamics.
The framework uses the joint distribution in unlabeled network data to support learning the relationship between topology and dynamics for resilience prediction.
The authors open-source the framework's code.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present TDNetGen as a novel resilience prediction framework for complex networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three network datasets reportedly achieve prediction accuracy of up to 85%-95%.
The framework reportedly retains pronounced augmentation capability in extreme low-data regimes.
The authors report that the framework enhances network resilience prediction utility and robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Network resilience prediction is important for understanding and improving complex systems under perturbations and failures.
Existing theoretical methods depend on prior dynamics knowledge, while data-driven methods face insufficient labeled data.
TDNetGen addresses the data limitation through generative augmentation of topology and dynamics, using unlabeled-data joint distributions.
The authors report 85%-95% accuracy on three datasets and augmentation capability in extreme low-data regimes.
The code is reported as open-sourced.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the network datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, or detailed model architecture.
The abstract does not report how accuracy varies across datasets or low-data regimes.
The abstract does not provide evidence of independent verification or reproducibility beyond the code link.
